svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: How one grid of ramp positions becomes a frame of RGB565 bytes
svg.desc: The glyph atlas, the grid of ramp positions, the gather that fills a four-dimensional array, the transpose that turns it into a picture, and the two bytes each pixel becomes.
svg.text: One grid of ramp positions, one frame of RGB565
Nothing is drawn per cell: the glyphs were drawn once, and a frame is a copy, a swap and some arithmetic.
every character of the ramp, rasterised once
rebuilt on a ramp, invert or font-size change,
64 x 24 cells, one ramp position each
1,536 of them, from the same table the
24 x 64 x 10 x 5 - cell rows, cell columns,
then the pixel rows and columns inside each
one numpy operation, where a text call per cell
would be 1,536 of them a frame
as gathered: a cell's ten pixel rows
sit together, which is not a picture
five bits of red and blue, six of green, high byte first
greyscale packs straight from the coverage channel, because red, green and blue are then the same
number - a three-channel image is never built. Colour blends the cell colour towards the unlit screen.
the driver's buffer is 4 KB, so a frame cannot
go in one call. About 33 ms, against 3.7 ms of
drawing - which is why none of it is per cell
